title: Japan's Everyday Foods Get a Protein Boost
paragraphs: In Japan, more and more food companies are adding extra protein to everyday foods, such as curry and coffee. This is because people are becoming more aware of the importance of protein for their health.

For example, in June 2026, the food company House Foods released a ready-to-eat curry in a pouch. It contains 30 grams of protein, which is about half of the amount that people need each day. The protein comes from chicken breast and protein powder. The company wants people to see curry as a food that is both tasty and healthy.

Another company, Maisen Fine Food, sells small pieces of soy protein that people can add to rice while it is cooking. It has received questions about the product from families, lunch box shops and companies that make school lunches.

Meiji, a large food company, sells a drink made with milk protein and vegetables. It is popular with single working people in their 20s. From June, Meiji also tested a coffee with 10 grams of protein and no sugar or fat for about six weeks. Meiji says it wants to encourage people to eat protein every day.

Protein products are also easy to find in convenience stores. For example, a protein shake made by the company ULTORA has been sold at FamilyMart stores since March 2026. According to the market research company Innova Market Insights, protein in Japan is moving away from supplements and into familiar foods and drinks.
According to a report by the research company Fuji Keizai, Japan's protein supplement market was expected to reach 309.6 billion yen in 2025, almost three times more than ten years earlier.
